players.note: Fred Warner showed up in Week 6, tallying six solos and two assists. He has three spike weeks and one splash week under his belt, placing him as the LB10 through six weeks of action. Tap Warner as a top-five option for Week 7, thanks to a plus matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Ernest Jones was excellent in Week 6, racking up five solos, four assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Jones has three spike weeks and one splash week to his name, helping propel him to the LB1 in total fantasy points through six weeks of play.

Alex Singleton stayed hot in Week 6, notching four solos, nine assists, and one tackle for loss. Singleton has five spike weeks and one near miss in his six contests, making him an easy top-12 play. The LB6 through six weeks of action, Singleton is a must-start regardless of opponent and should be treated as such for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

Nakobe Dean stayed hot in Week 6, tallying three solos, nine assists, and one tackle for loss. Dean has three spike weeks and two splash weeks, vaulting him to LB2 overall status through six weeks of action. Dean has earned the right to be counted as a top-five option going forward and should be treated as such for a suddenly plus matchup against a banged-up Los Angeles Rams team in Week 7.

Josiah Trotter kept the fire burning in Week 6, racking up five solos, seven assists, and one pass defended. The LB8 overall despite missing a game, Trotter has four spike weeks and one splash week in five games. Treat him as a top-five option at the position until he gives us a reason not to. Fire him up with confidence for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Carson Schwesinger was excellent in Week 6, reeling off five solos, eight assists, and one forced fumble. Schwesinger has remained in the LB1 mix due to two spike weeks and a splash week, but is being outshined by several other names. Still, he is providing a solid return on his draft day investment and is a strong top-10 option for Week 7 and beyond. Treat him as such for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Devin Lloyd has been an IDP monster when he has been on the field, recording three spike weeks and one mega splash week in his four games played. In Week 6, he posted three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Easily the LB1 overall in fppg, Lloyd is a must-start who should be considered part of the top-five conversation from here on out. Lloyd is legit. Fire him up with confidence for a pus Week 7 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Payton Wilson stayed hot in Week 6, tallying seven solos and four assists. Wilson, the LB4 overall through six weeks of play, has two splash weeks and three spike weeks in just six contests, locking him into the top-five conversation until further notice. Production like this cannot be ignored. Tap Payton as just that for a plus Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints in Paris.

Blake Cashman stayed hot in Week 5, reeling off five solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. The LB6 on the season, Cashman has four spike weeks to his name and may finally be ready to get the widespread IDP recognition he deserves for his consistency and upside. Tap Cashman as a top-12 option for Week 7 and beyond.

Jacob Rodriguez stayed hot in Week 5, tallying four solos and seven assists. Rodriguez has three spike weeks to his name, which has helped vault him to LB4 overall prior to the Dolphins' Week 6 bye. Tap the impressive rookie linebacker as a top-10 option for a plus Week 7 matchup against the New York Jets.

Anthony Hill showed up in Week 6, racking three solos, six assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Hill has been a strong LB3 option, thanks to three spike weeks. The Titans rookie can be counted as a top-25 option for Week 7, thanks to a tasty matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Jamien Sherwood showed up in Week 6, registering six solos, five assists, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. Sherwood has two spike weeks to his name, helping push him to LB14 status through six weeks of play. Tap Sherwood as a top-20 option for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Quay Walker stepped up in Week 6, recording three solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Quay has three spike weeks under his belt on the season, keeping him in the top-25 mix for the bye weeks. Tap him as an LB2 play for a plus Week 7 matchup against the banged-up Los Angeles Rams.

Jack Campbell stepped up in Week 5, tallying five solos and six assists. Campbell has three spike weeks to his name with four or more solos in four of his five games but has dropped to the LB2 discussion due to Derrick Barnes siphoning some of his tackle upside and weekly fantasy production. He should be back to being a top-12 option sooner rather than later, but should be counted as a top-20 option for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Demario Davis was at it again in Week 6, tallying six solos, one assist, and one pass defended. The LB31 on the season thanks to two spike weeks and one splash week in his last four games. Demario is a top-25 play during the byes and should be treated as such for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris.

Quincy Williams was at it again in Week 6, tallying four solos, two assists, and one sack. Williams has started to heat up, registering two spike weeks and one splash week in his last four games. The LB15 on the season, treat Quincy as a top-12 option for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Bobby Okereke was excellent in Week 6, tallying seven solos, one assist, one sack, three tackles for loss, and two passes defended. Okereke has been a strong LB2 option, recording four or more solos in three of his five contests. The LB22 through five weeks of action, treat the Panthers linebacker as a top-25 option for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Barrett Carter was excellent in Week 5, reeling off five solos, six assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Carter has recorded five or more solos in three of his five games, but managed just two solos in the other two, keeping him in LB2 territory. Tap him as a top-20 option for Week 7.

Pete Werner stepped up in Week 6, racking up five solos, six assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended on 100 percent of the snaps. Werner now has two spike weeks to his name and is playing a full-time role with Kaden Elliss sidelined. An LB3 when Elliss is healthy, and he is splitting snaps with Danny Stutsman, Werner is a high-end LB2 option with Kaden injured. Werner has recorded four or more solos in three of his last five games. Treat Werner as a top-20 option until Elliss returns, at which point he will go back to being a top-36 option.

Demetrius Knight was excellent in Week 5, reeling off five solos, three assists, and two tackles for loss. Knight has two spike weeks and one splash week to his name, making him a top-25 option, especially during the byes. Treat him as such for Week 7.

Jaden Dugger impressed again in Week 6, notching eight solos and three assists on 100 percent of the snaps. Dugger was a hit from a fantasy perspective, but his struggles in coverage ensure that he won't be unseating Dre Greenlaw (suspended for Week 6) anytime soon. The back-to-back spike weeks as a starter make him a dynasty stash for 2027 and beyond, but it will take another suspension or injury before Dugger is fantasy relevant again this season. Look elsewhere for Week 7.

Henry To'oTo'o returned to action in Week 6, posting three solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. To'oTo'o had been sidelined since Week 1 with Jake Hansen filling in for him. To'oTo'o becomes an immediate LB3 candidate who will return to the LB2 conversation once he gets his legs back under him and shows some consistency. Tap the Texans linebacker as a top-30 option for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the New York Giants.

Derrick Barnes was excellent in Week 5, racking up three solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Barnes has been elite this season with three spike weeks and one splash week to his name, but is still good to count as more of a top-15 option than a top-10 one due to posting a dud in the other game. Treat him as such for Week 7.

Ty'Ron Hopper was solid in Week 6, generating three solos, two assists, and one pass defended on 42 percent of the snaps. Hopper looked like the Packer who was going to lead the position group in snaps alongside Zaire Franklin, but in Week 6, Isaiah McDuffie played 55 percent of the snaps. It appears that both Hopper and McDuffie will rotate in place of the injured Edgerrin Cooper, essentially cannibalizing each other's fantasy values in the process. They both will provide some start-worthy stat lines over the course of the rest of the season, but predicting who will when becomes a futile exercise as long as they are in a platoon-type situation. Keep him stashed in deeper formats, but look elsewhere for Week 7.

Nick Herbig finally showed up in Week 6, racking up six solos, two sacks, and three tackles for loss. Herbig is a clear backup to T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith but often gets enough snaps to make an impact, as he can play against both the run and the pass. The sacks were the first of the season for Herbig, who has been solid for a bench piece and has started to heat up during the byes. Tap Herbig as a DL3 with a DL4 floor for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

Jeremiah Trotter stepped up in Week 6, racking up four solos, two assists, and 0.5 sacks on 36 percent of the snaps. Trotter saw an expanded role in Week 6, with Jihaad Campbell being demoted due to issues in coverage. This may be a long-term ascension as the Eagles are looking for a spark on defense and are tired of opposing teams targeting Jihaad in coverage.  Trotter becomes an immediate LB3 with LB2 upside as long as he is receiving starter snaps, and can jump into the LB2 conversation once we are certain his snaps will not fluctuate too wildly on a week-to-week basis. Tap Trotter as a top-30 option for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football.

Kendal Williams was excellent in Week 6, notching six solos, one assist, and one tackle for loss. Kendal was rushed to a local hospital in Atlanta following a scary third quarter collision but was released by the end of the game, where he was spotted walking around under his own power. Williams has recorded back-to-back spike weeks and has emerged as a strong LB3 option with LB2 upside for the bye weeks. Kendal is an add regardless of his injury status, but those looking to put in a FAAB bid should factor the injury into their bid amount. Tap Williams as a top-30 option for Week 7 against San Francisco if he is active.

David Walker stepped up in Week 6, tallying four solos, three assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss on 32 percent of the snaps. Walker is now up to four sacks on the season with at least one sack in three of his last five games. Walker has been the Buccaneers' most productive edge player but has yet to attain starter-level snaps. That could change in a hurry, but for now we can only trust the Bucs edge rusher as a flex2 type as opposed to the DL3 type his sack production and obvious talent suggest.

Jonathan Cooper has been removed from the Commissioner's exempt list, making him worth a speculative add in all formats. I say "speculative" because there is still a chance Cooper receives a suspension from the NFL. Cooper will be a DL3 when he first returns and will re-join the DL2 conversation once he gets a sack or two under his belt.
